extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in mathematical physics, symplectic geometry, and BRST/geometric quantization
extracted.subtask_description: Technical construction and analysis of the classical BRST complex, its Poisson structure, relation to vertical (leafwise) cohomology, and the beginnings of geometric (pre)quantization. Covers existence/inductive construction of the BRST differential, its realization as an (inner) Poisson derivation, and topological conditions determining BRST cohomology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of BRST derivations δ_i with D^2=0
rubrics_metrics.description: We can define derivations D = Σ_i δ_i on K, where δ_i have bidegree (i,i−1), such that D^2 = 0. (Theorem III.2.14: We can define a derivation D = Σ_{i=0}^∞ δ_i on K, where δ_i are derivations of bidegree (i,i−1), such that D^2 = 0.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct δ_0 (Koszul differential) and δ_1 (vertical derivative on functions/ghosts), then inductively solve for higher δ_i using the filtration F_pK and the quasi-acyclicity of the Koszul complex so that partial sums D^k = Σ_{i=0}^k δ_i are nilpotent up to higher filtration degree until full nilpotency D^2=0 is achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasi-acyclicity of the Koszul complex
rubrics_metrics.description: The Koszul complex ... −→ K_2 δ_0 −→ K_1 δ_0 −→ K_0 → 0 is (quasi-)acyclic in the sense used to inductively construct δ_i and prove existence lemmas. (Lemma III.2.15 and surrounding text.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This quasi-acyclicity (acyclicity on positive b-degree) is the algebraic hypothesis used to deduce existence of higher δ_i and of homotopy K solving d = [δ_0, K]. It is invoked repeatedly to show cocycles are coboundaries at the required filtration degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: BRST total differential D induces vertical cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the BRST construction is to lift the vertical derivative to K. The total differential D = δ_0 + δ_1 + δ_2 + ... has cohomology isomorphic to the vertical cohomology (Theorem III.2.18: classical BRST cohomology H^n_D ≅ H^n_V(M_0) for n ≥ 0 and zero for n < 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because all δ_i have non-negative filtration degree, the spectral sequence of the filtration has E1 = Koszul cohomology and E2 = vertical cohomology; higher differentials vanish for degree reasons, yielding the claimed identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: BRST operator should be a Poisson derivation (inner if possible)
rubrics_metrics.description: K is a Poisson superalgebra and the BRST operator D can (and should be defined to) be a Poisson derivation. There exists Q ∈ K^1 with #Q,Q# = 0 and D = #Q,·#. (Theorems III.3.19–III.3.20.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct Q = Σ_i Q_i by matching bidegrees: Q_0 produces the Koszul differential, Q_1 gives δ_1, etc. Using the filtration and quasi-acyclicity, solve inductively so that #Q,Q# = 0; then D = #Q,·# is automatically nilpotent and its cohomology inherits Poisson structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical choice of Q_0 and Q_1 matching δ_0 and δ_1
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a unique element Q_0 ∈ K^{1,0} with #Q_0, b_i# = δ_0 b_i = φ_i (Q_0 = Σ_i c^i φ_i). There is a unique Q_1 ∈ K^{2,1} such that #Q_1, c_i# = δ_1 c_i (Q_1 = −(1/2) Σ_{i,j,k} f_{ijk} c^i ∧ c^j ∧ b_k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These choices ensure that the induced action on generators reproduces δ_0 and δ_1; higher Q_i are then obtained inductively to kill higher-order obstructions (R_1^2, R_2^2, ... in the filtration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure of constraints (group action) simplifies BRST (finite truncation)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the constraints close under the Poisson bracket (e.g., they are the components of a moment map for a group action with constant structure constants f_{ijk}), then δ_1^2 = 0 and the higher δ_i (i > 1) are not necessary; Q = Q_0 + Q_1 suffices (III.3.23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this group-action case the BRST operator reduces to the standard Batalin–Vilkovisky/Batalin–Fradkin–Vilkovisky form and the BRST cohomology is identified with Lie algebra cohomology H(g; C^∞(M_0)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Poisson superalgebra axioms for K
rubrics_metrics.description: K = C^∞(M) ⊗ Λ(V ⊕ V^*) must be a Z_2-graded associative supercommutative algebra with a Poisson bracket obeying (P1) associative supercommutativity, (P2) Lie superalgebra identities, and (P3) bracket as derivation over multiplication (III.3.(P1)-(P3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ghost/antighost exterior algebra with bracket induced from dual pairing extends to all of K as an odd derivation; checking (P1)-(P3) ensures the BRST constructions respect Poisson structure and that inner derivations behave as claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology inherits Poisson (and graded) structure
rubrics_metrics.description: If D = #Q,·# is an (inner) Poisson derivation with D^2 = 0, then ker D is a Poisson subalgebra, im D a Poisson ideal, and HD = ker D / im D inherits the structure of a Poisson superalgebra and graded Poisson module; in particular H^0_D ≅ C^∞(reduced M) (III.3.20–III.3.21).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This justifies computing reduced Poisson brackets by computing representatives in K and projecting to cohomology; cohomological observables therefore form a Poisson algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertical (leafwise) cohomology interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: The classical BRST cohomology is the vertical de Rham cohomology acting on differential forms along the leaves of the null foliation M_⊥0 defined by i^*Ω; the vertical derivative d_V has cohomology H_V(M_0) and the BRST cohomology equals this (Section 4 introduction and Theorem III.2.18).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One computes vertical forms Ω^{p,0} and uses the vertical d_V; local Poincaré lemma holds along fibers under the usual fiberwise hypotheses, yielding the identification of BRST cohomology with sheaf cohomology of π_*E and with sections of an associated bundle whose fiber is H(F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Topological criteria linking fiber cohomology to vertical cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: Buchdahl-type results: H^1(F)=0 implies H^1_V(M_0)=0; if H^{p-1}(F)=H^p(F)=0 for p>1 then H^p_V(M_0)=0. Conversely, vanishing of adjacent vertical cohomology implies vanishing of fiber cohomology (Theorems III.4.5–III.4.6, Corollary III.4.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These give necessary and sufficient conditions for vanishing of BRST cohomology in positive ghost number in terms of the de Rham cohomology of the typical fiber (gauge orbit). Use these to deduce existence/nonexistence of nontrivial cohomology classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: BRST cohomology depends only on constrained submanifold (not constraint presentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The BRST cohomology does not depend on the explicit form of the constraints but only on the constrained submanifold i: M_0 → M (Theorem III.4.17 and following discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although complexes used to compute it differ with choices (e.g., connections), the resulting vertical cohomology (and hence BRST cohomology) is invariant; practically, one may choose any convenient connection/representation to compute it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of BRST cohomology as sections of an associated bundle
rubrics_metrics.description: As a C^∞(reduced M)-module, the BRST cohomology is isomorphic to smooth sections of the associated bundle M_0 ×_ρ H(F) → reduced M, where ρ: Diff F → Aut H(F) is the representation on fiber cohomology (Theorem III.4.17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local triviality yields HV(U) ≅ C^∞(U) ⊗ H(F); transition functions act via the induced automorphisms on H(F). In the principal G-bundle case with connected G, the associated bundle is trivial and HV ≅ C^∞(reduced M) ⊗ H(G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact, orientable fibers give Poincaré duality in vertical cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: If the typical fiber F is n-dimensional, compact and orientable (indeed parallelizable in the irreducible case), then Poincaré duality yields an isomorphism H^p_V(M_0) ≅ H^{n−p}_V(M_0) (Corollary III.4.23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This duality follows from the fiberwise Poincaré duality H^p(F) ≅ H^{n−p}(F) and the local-product description HV(U×F) ≅ C^∞(U) ⊗ H(F). Use to relate ghost-number graded pieces of BRST cohomology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrality condition for prequantization
rubrics_metrics.description: A symplectic form Ω is prequantizable iff its de Rham class is integral: [Ω] lies in the image of H^2(M; Z) → H^2_{dR}(M; R) (IV.1.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When this integrality holds there exists a complex Hermitian line bundle E → M with connection ∇ whose curvature satisfies curv(∇) = −2π i Ω; this data is required to construct the prequantum Hilbert space and the prequantization operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prequantization map properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Given prequantum data (E,∇,⟨·,·⟩) define O(f) = ∇_{X_f} + 2π i f acting on Γ(E). The map satisfies [O(f), O(g)] = O({f,g}), the Leibniz relation O(f)(gσ) = {f,g} σ + g O(f)σ, and O(f) is skew-symmetric on the natural L^2-domain (IV.1.6–IV.1.9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these properties to realize C^∞(M) (under Poisson bracket) as skew-symmetric operators in the prequantum Hilbert space. This representation is reducible; polarizations are used to reduce to a physically meaningful quantum space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polarization choice for irreducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A polarization F is an involutive Lagrangian complex subbundle of T_C M (a complex, involutive, Lagrangian distribution). Choosing a polarization selects the subspace of sections constant along the polarization directions to reduce the prequantum representation to an irreducible one (Section on Polarizations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polarizations can be real (F = C ⊗ V for real Lagrangian V) or totally complex (F ∩ F̄ = 0, giving an almost complex structure J with J^2 = −1 and integrability conditions). Existence and invariance of polarizations impose constraints; invariant polarizations may force compatible choices in ghost sector when applying BRST quantization.

rubrics_metrics.name: BRST prequantization compatibility condition
rubrics_metrics.description: If (M,Ω) is prequantizable then pulling back the prequantum line bundle to M_0 yields a Hermitian line bundle whose connection is flat along null foliation directions; hence the smooth sections admit a representation of vector fields tangent to the foliation and one can build a BRST cohomology theory for sections—except inner product/integration issues (Section on BRST prequantization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All prequantum data induce corresponding BRST data `à la BRST' except the inner product which involves integration over reduced space; one must address analytic/integration problems separately when constructing the quantum BRST Hilbert space.
